topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course themes, personal background, and core learning goals regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: The Biological Nature of Cancer and Mutation Drivers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease shaped by the microenvironment and outline the intrinsic and extrinsic forces driving cellular mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Risk Factors and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate known environmental exposures, public perception of cancer etiology, and geographic epidemiological patterns to demonstrate the environmental contribution to cancer incidence.

topics.label: Oncogenic Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how infectious agents drive malignancy, using Burkitt lymphoma to illustrate the interaction between geographic infection patterns, immunosuppression, and oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific physical agents and metabolized chemical compounds cause direct DNA damage, bulky adducts, and mutational transversions.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Host Context, and Carcinogenic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic aspects of carcinogenesis, focusing on the role of promoters, chronic inflammation, developmental susceptibility, and summarizing these integrated mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Everyday Risk Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with final remarks on balancing exposure risks against everyday benefits.
